survey: A western saddle sits on a horizontal wooden fence rail, with a post at the right edge of the full card. The saddle's length runs along the rail. The horn and pommel are at the left (front) end and a tall rounded cantle is at the right (back) end. The curved seat has a lighter padded insert and sits on top of the tree, which rests on the rail. Flat rectangular skirts hang down on both sides of the rail: the near skirt faces the camera, and the far skirt shows behind it on the right. The rail runs between the two skirts, going in on the left and coming out on the right. Its width and perspective are consistent, and the right end is closer to the camera. A stitched leather fender strap hangs from the middle of the near side and runs through a metal buckle into the top bar of the near stirrup. The far stirrup hangs behind it, shifted right and up. That shift matches the far skirt's position in this three-quarter view. Its strap is hidden behind the near skirt, and only a short stub shows above the stirrup. Both stirrups are wide western-style treads and hang freely. There is no cinch or girth. On a saddle resting on a rail that is an acceptable simplification. In the full card the rail passes in front of the post and rests against it.
